issues.legal_issue: A family arrangement that allocates income from property for family members’ maintenance does not effect a partition unless its terms show an unequivocal intention to divide the property into defined shares.
material_facts: The instrument described the allocations as amounts for family members’ maintenance and assigned income from groups of properties to them.
The instrument did not unequivocally declare an intention to partition or define the coparceners’ shares.
The income allocations differed substantially, including a much smaller allocation to one son than to the other.

The revenue authority had also relied on evidence of separate accounts, realisations, and possession, but the Board of Revenue did not address the instrument’s terms and the disparities in its allocations.
The dispute arose in tax assessments concerning whether the family property had been partitioned.
issues.conclusion: The instrument provided for maintenance and did not effect a partition. The assessments were therefore to proceed without giving effect to it as a partition deed, and the appeals were dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Whether an instrument effects a partition depends on its terms and substance. An unequivocal intention to partition and defined shares are absent where the instrument expressly provides maintenance, allocates income rather than property shares, and makes allocations so disparate that they are inconsistent with a partition of joint family property. Evidence of separate accounts, realisations, and possession does not prevent the High Court from reaching an independent conclusion where the revenue authority failed to construe the instrument properly and consider relevant circumstances. The Court affirmed the High Court’s conclusion in the statutory reference concerning assessments under Section 24(1) of the United Provinces Agricultural Income Tax Act, 1948, as modified and extended, and the questions concerning the restriction in Section 24(1) of the Rewa State Land Revenue and Tenancy Code, 1935. No earlier cases were relied on.

rule.if: tax_assessment_dispute and instrument_allocates_maintenance_income and not unequivocal_partition_intent and shares_not_defined and substantially_unequal_allocations

predicates.tax_assessment_dispute: The dispute concerns tax assessments that depend on whether family property was partitioned.
predicates.instrument_allocates_maintenance_income: The instrument allocates income from property to family members for their maintenance rather than allotting property shares.
predicates.unequivocal_partition_intent: The instrument unequivocally expresses an intention to partition the property.
predicates.shares_not_defined: The instrument does not define the family members’ shares in the property.
predicates.substantially_unequal_allocations: The instrument makes substantially unequal allocations of income to family members.

issues.definition: When a tax assessment dispute concerns an instrument that allocates maintenance income without an unequivocal intention to partition or defined shares, and its allocations are substantially unequal, the instrument does not effect a partition.
